explanation.title: One-factor absorption ratio (AR1)
explanation.measure: The share of total cross-asset movement explained by the single largest common factor.
explanation.simple: If AR1 is 40%, one broad force—such as liquidity, rates, inflation, or fear—explains about 40% of the movement across all 24 assets.
explanation.portfolio: A high or rapidly rising value means diversification is becoming more dependent on one macro driver.

explanation.title: Top-three absorption ratio (AR3)
explanation.measure: The share of total movement explained by the three largest common factors.
explanation.simple: If AR3 is 65%, most of the market is responding to only three broad forces.
explanation.portfolio: A high value means many apparently different positions may still be concentrated in a few macro bets.

explanation.title: Effective rank / effective bets
explanation.measure: An estimate of how many statistically independent sources of risk remain in the 24-asset universe.
explanation.simple: A reading of 8 means 24 tickers currently behave more like eight genuinely different bets.
explanation.portfolio: A falling value warns that the number of holdings may overstate actual diversification.

explanation.title: Dominant-factor ratio (spectral gap)
explanation.measure: How large the first eigenvalue is compared with the second eigenvalue.
explanation.simple: A reading of 3x means the strongest common factor is about three times as powerful as the next factor.
explanation.portfolio: A high value suggests one theme is dominating the whole market.

explanation.title: Matrix instability (condition number)
explanation.measure: The ratio between the strongest and weakest risk directions in the correlation matrix.
explanation.simple: A high value is like a table whose weight is concentrated on one leg: small data changes can create large model changes.
explanation.portfolio: High instability reduces confidence in optimized weights and fine-tuned allocation outputs.

explanation.title: Common factor above random noise
explanation.measure: How far the largest eigenvalue sits above the Marchenko-Pastur random-noise boundary.
explanation.simple: A positive excess suggests the common factor is too large to be explained by random correlations alone.
explanation.portfolio: A large excess strengthens the case that the observed herding is economically meaningful.

explanation.title: Strong-connection share (edge density)
explanation.measure: The fraction of all 276 unique asset pairs with absolute correlation above 0.50.
explanation.simple: A reading of 46% means roughly 127 of 276 pairs have a strong relationship.
explanation.portfolio: A high or rising value means shocks can spread across more of the portfolio.

explanation.title: Clustering coefficient
explanation.measure: How often strongly linked assets form tightly connected groups or triangles.
explanation.simple: If SPY links to QQQ and XLK, and QQQ also links to XLK, they form a tight cluster.
explanation.portfolio: Dense clusters can reveal duplicate exposures that look diversified only because they use different tickers.

explanation.title: 60-day drawdown
explanation.measure: How far SPY is below its highest close in the last 60 trading days.
explanation.simple: A -10% reading means SPY is 10% below its two-to-three-month high.
explanation.portfolio: A deep drawdown can create rebound potential while also indicating an unstable market.

explanation.title: Price versus 50-day moving average
explanation.measure: The percentage distance between SPY and its 50-day average price.
explanation.simple: A -5% reading means SPY trades 5% below its medium-term trend.
explanation.portfolio: Below-trend prices can confirm weakness or create rebound potential depending on the wider regime.

explanation.title: 20-day realised volatility
explanation.measure: The annualised variability of daily SPY returns over the last 20 trading days.
explanation.simple: Higher realised volatility means the market is making larger daily moves than usual.
explanation.portfolio: It can confirm stress, but it often reacts after fragility has already increased.

explanation.title: Cross-asset breadth
explanation.measure: The share of the 24 assets trading above their own 20-day moving averages.
explanation.simple: A 25% reading means only six of 24 assets are above their short-term trends.
explanation.portfolio: Narrow breadth makes a headline-index rally less trustworthy.

explanation.title: 60-day drawdown
explanation.measure: How far SPY is below its highest close in the last 60 trading days.
explanation.simple: A -10% reading means SPY is 10% below its two-to-three-month high.
explanation.portfolio: A deep drawdown can create rebound potential while also indicating an unstable market.

explanation.title: 20-day drawdown
explanation.measure: How far SPY is below its highest close in the last 20 trading days.
explanation.simple: It measures shorter-horizon damage and oversold conditions.
explanation.portfolio: A deep reading can raise mean-reversion potential, but should be read with crash risk.

explanation.title: Five-day return / short-term reversal
explanation.measure: SPY's total return over the last five trading days.
explanation.simple: A positive rebound after a drawdown may strengthen a rally setup.
explanation.portfolio: The signal is more credible when breadth and credit also improve.
